question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [British settlements and presidencies in mid-18th century India]
options: Madras Presidency — centered at Fort St. George on the Coromandel Coast
Bengal Presidency — centered at Fort William on the Hooghly River
Bombay Presidency — centered at Bombay Castle on the western coast
Bencoolen (Fort Marlborough) — British settlement in India near Madras
wrong_fact: Bencoolen (Fort Marlborough) was a British East India Company settlement in Sumatra (modern Indonesia), NOT in India near Madras.
explanation: In the mid-18th century, the British East India Company was structured around three main Presidencies in India: Madras (Fort St. George), Bombay (Bombay Castle), and Bengal (Fort William). Bencoolen (Fort Marlborough) was an important British presidency and pepper trading port located in Sumatra, Indonesia, which was administered by the Company but was not in India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [British factories and strategic outposts on the east coast of India before 1756]
options: Injaram factory — British cloth-weaving factory in the Godavari delta
Vizagapatam (Visakhapatnam) — British fortified factory on the Northern Circars coast
Devikottai — Fortified post at the mouth of the Coleroon River acquired by the British
Masulipatam (Machilipatnam) — British primary military headquarters on the Malabar coast
wrong_fact: Masulipatam (Machilipatnam) is located on the Coromandel Coast (eastern coast) of India, not the Malabar coast (western coast).
explanation: During the Carnatic Wars, Masulipatam was a highly contested trading port and factory on the Coromandel Coast of modern Andhra Pradesh, not the Malabar Coast (which is Kerala/western coast). Injaram, Vizagapatam, and Devikottai were key British footholds and factories on the eastern side of the peninsula.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical extent of British and rival French spheres of influence in 1750–1754]
options: Northern Circars — territory assigned to the French under Bussy, stretching along the Andhra coast
Gingee — French-occupied hill fort dominating the Carnatic interior
Tanjore — neutral Danish settlement serving as a buffer state between Madras and Pondicherry
Fort St. David — British stronghold located just south of Pondicherry at Cuddalore
wrong_fact: Tanjore (Thanjavur) was an independent Maratha kingdom, not a Danish settlement. The main Danish settlement in the Carnatic region was Tranquebar (Tharangambadi).
explanation: During the Second Carnatic War, the Northern Circars were leased/assigned to the French under Bussy, and Gingee was a major French stronghold. Fort St. David at Cuddalore was a key British base. Tanjore was a Maratha principality ruled by the Bhonsle dynasty, which was courted by both British and French forces, whereas Tranquebar was the Danish trading settlement in the area.
